text:
kevin: Heads-up — running into propagation delays for the Private/VPC canary. Canaries are configured to 5% but some air-gapped tenants show 0% after control-plane update. Anyone seen this pattern?
sarah: saw something like this last quarter. usually a sync agent on the customer side fell behind or rejected a signed manifest. any errors in the control-plane logs?
maria: looking at the control-plane audit: we emitted a signed manifest and status=delivered, but the per-tenant sync reports 'manifest_stale' later. suspect clock skew or replay guard.
kevin: exact error from tenant agent: "signature verification failed: key rotation mismatch" — they rotated KMS and didn't fetch new public key. air-gapped makes key distribution tricky.
alex: that explains it. For air-gapped installs we currently rely on 'pull' sync: tenant agent pulls manifests from our ICP (internal config plane) via a customer-side S3 mirror. If their mirror didn't get the rotated key bundle, agent rejects.
sarah: hmm. two pieces to fix: 1) prevent control-plane from advancing canary if any tenant reports manifest_rejects; 2) improve console UX to surface per-tenant propagation + reason.
kevin: proposal: add a propagation-guard stage. New rollout state machine: APPROVE -> PUBLISH_MANIFEST -> WAIT_PROPAGATION(window=10m) -> VERIFY_SIGNED(state) -> TRAFFIC_SHIFT. If any tenant reports reject during WAIT_PROPAGATION, auto-hold and send operator alert.
maria: +1. Also add a 'soft-fallback' where canary traffic split doesn't exceed 1% until VERIFY_SIGNED passes for all targeted tenants. That reduces blast radius while still exercising path.
alex: sketch of YAML for rollout config i've been testing:
```yaml
rollout: canary-2026-03
traffic:
  stable: 95
  canary: 5
guards:
  max_error_rate: 0.03
  propagation_window: 600 # seconds
  require_manifest_ack: true
  min_tenants_verified: 100%
```
kevin: love the min_tenants_verified flag. For private installs we should allow 'min_tenants_verified: by-tenant-list' because some customers want staged rollouts per VPC.
sarah: console notes: we need three new telemetry metrics exposed per rollout: manifests_emitted, manifests_applied, manifests_failed. Also show estimated propagation completion time per region/VPC. Operators currently guess.
deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Rollout canary-2026-03 published to control-plane at 1766123460.
ops-bot: [ops-bot] Alert created: tenant 'acme-corp' manifest_reject — signature mismatch. Ticket #INC-4821.
maria: For air-gapped constraints we should support an out-of-band signed bundle exchange: control-plane publishes signed bundle + rotation hints; customer operator can import via console upload if automatic mirror unfurls fail. UX: console should show a one-click 'generate import bundle' and an upload token valid for 24h.
alex: +1, and the bundle should include a delta-only manifest to keep transfer small for low-bandwidth sites.
kevin: operational guard: if >1 tenant in target list rejects more than 5% manifests in window, rollback to previous model variant automatically. We must be explicit in SLA docs.
sarah: also consider drift detection: agents should report applied_manifest_hash; control-plane can diff and surface 'drifted-configs' if local changes exist. That reduces confusion when customer modifies routing locally.
maria: quick follow-up: we need a dashboard card in Rollouts page: "Propagation health" with heatmap, per-tenant last_applied_ts, and quick actions: resend bundle, generate import bundle, mark-ack-exempt (with audit).
kevin: ok next steps: 1) I'll draft state machine PR for propagation-guard. 2) @maria can you mock the UX card? 3) @alex can you add require_manifest_ack toggle to rollout API. Aim to ship a beta to staging by EOW.
alex: will add API flag and test harness for airgap mirror failures.
maria: will mock and toss on Figma + annotation for devs.
sarah: i'll add the three telemetry metrics to the tracing/ingest plan and wire alerts for >2 tenant rejects in 10m.
kevin: thanks. if anyone hits tenant timeouts >12m, reply here and i'll escalate to success team. :thumbsup:
